## Round 6 (source-layer report from rendering docs/prime; audit passed at revision_5)
- Item 1 (refunds that come off a duplicate refund; posting target when earlier payments are returned): real. Rules now match the compute: "Refunds already issued against the latest payment posted against the refunded installment / first installment charge come off its excess"; the baseline sentences say "less the refunds already issued against that latest payment"; the posting sentences now read "is posted against the latest payment posted against the refunded installment (first installment charge) and goes back through that payment's method", so the target payment and method are defined on every rung of the payment-returned ladder. Compute unchanged.
- Item 2 (paying ahead): real. rp_last_start replaced by rp_last_end (latest coverage_period_end of a charge), so "no installment covers a month after the current month" is tested on coverage end as the rule says. Check: quarterly first installment Oct-Dec -> no installment paid ahead.
- Item 3 (Select with no disenrollment date): real. Rules now state it: catch-up and supplement - a month lies wholly inside an open-ended Select enrollment when it falls after its effective month, and "touched" means containing the effective or the disenrollment date; credit - coverage runs every month from its effective month on where it has no disenrollment date (prerequisite condition updated to match). Compute: cu_s_hi, su_s_hi, cr_s_hi use an open upper bound (99999) instead of the current month, so the current month is no longer counted as touched.
- Item 5 (effective-month days in the supplement baseline): real. Baseline and the otherwise rung now say "through the last day of the coverage period of the installment charge beginning on the effective date, 30 where no such charge stands".
- Item 6 (draft excess): real for a drafted installment that is also the latest-coverage installment and starts inside the history. dd_chg_w now always takes the drafted installment's in-history charge out (zero when it starts after the history ends).
- Item 4: base issue, not touched.
- Scored values unchanged in both tasks (task 0 113.54 / 17.98 / 45.02 / 65.02; task 1 32.51 / 24.98 / 16.01 / 48.52); factor sensitivities unchanged; six orders per task give one hash. Proof text updated (refund posting basis, initial_months_ahead evidence now cites coverage end). task_tools.py not changed this round. Full gate block green including check_traceability (0.json 22 copied / 0 missing; 1.json 21 / 0).

## Round 8 (rework from audits revision_7: N15, O-r7b)
- Read the revision_7 sections of _difficulty.md, 0.md and 1.md in full.
- N15 (draft gate reads two ways when the duplicate refund lands on a first installment and refunds nothing):
  - Picking "among non-first installments only" cannot be computed in the policy DSL (MAX/LATEST filter by equality only, so a largest payment cannot be taken over every installment but one). The gate was made single-reading instead, and the first-installment exclusion was narrowed so the duplicate refund refunds nothing far less often.
  - Draft prerequisite sentence (action form, fallback kept) is now "No draft is made on an account until the region has made the duplicate refund owed on it, wherever that refund comes to more than nothing." A 0.00 figure awaits no act; a positive figure awaits that refund. Condition and fallback_reason restated to match.
  - The duplicate refund is now idempotent, so "the refund owed" has one value: refunds already issued against the latest payment come off both the payment returned and the excess (rule d_prior/f_off, d_base2/f_base, d_final/f_final; compute MX(0, MN(pick - ref_ret, excess - ref_ret - kept))). Re-figured after task 0's own 17.98 refund, it gives 0.00.
  - Scope split by enrollment age: the duplicate refund now refunds nothing on a first installment charge only where the enrollment took effect in the current plan year, and the first-installment duplicate refund now refunds nothing where the enrollment took effect before it (rf_old). Each first-installment duplicate therefore has exactly one policy that refunds it. Auditor case H2 (2020 first installment with one 200.00 EFT payment): the duplicate refund concerns it and figures 0.00 (a single payment, no duplicate), so the draft waits on nothing; with the first installment paid twice, it refunds 164.98.
- O-r7b (payment look-back from mid-month vs charges from the first): left as an observation. A calendar-month cut on posting dates cannot be computed here, and moving the charges onto the same look-back would bucket a first-of-month charge by today's day. The rule states the behaviour exactly.
- Scored values unchanged (task 0 113.54 / 17.98 / 45.02 / 65.02; task 1 32.51 / 24.98 / 16.01 / 48.52). One factor sensitivity moved: duplicate_payment_returned 10.00 -> 8.00 (the 2.00 already refunded now comes off the payment returned); proof text updated. Six orders per task give one hash. task_tools.py unchanged. Full gate block green including check_traceability (22/0 and 21/0).

## Round 9 (rework from audits revision_8: N16 and the "which policy satisfies this state" class)
- Read the revision_8 sections of _difficulty.md, 0.md and 1.md in full.
- N16 (the draft's duplicate-refund gate could be met by either duplicate-refund policy; 7.53 vs 32.51 on task 1's records): closed by scope. The draft now draws nothing on an enrollment that took effect in the current plan year (r_scope + dd_new). The first-installment duplicate refund acts only on such enrollments (rf_old, round 8), so on every account the draft can act on, only the general duplicate refund can owe a refund. On task 1's records the draft now figures 0.00, one answer.
- Class sweep: for every prerequisite sentence, the policies whose writes can change the waited-on state were listed, and the scopes were split by the plan year the enrollment took effect in, so that exactly the declared resolver can act on any account where the blocked policy acts.
  - Before the current plan year: catch-up (new: cu_new; "no catch-up is charged on an enrollment that took effect in the current plan year"), duplicate refund (all installments of such an enrollment, first included), one-time payment (new: mp_new; "it settles no payment toward an enrollment that took effect in the current plan year"), draft (dd_new).
  - In the current plan year: first-installment supplement (new: su_old; "no supplement is charged on an enrollment that took effect before the current plan year"), first-installment duplicate refund (rf_old), initial payment (new: rp_out; "it settles nothing toward an enrollment that took effect before the current plan year"). The duplicate refund still acts on such enrollments' later installments but leaves their first installment alone.
  - Edges after the split:
    - draft <- catch-up (a charge reaching the month before the current month): only the catch-up (the supplement is current-year only).
    - draft <- duplicate refund: only the general refund.
    - draft <- one-time payment (current installment paid in full): only the one-time payment (the initial payment is current-year only).
    - initial payment <- supplement: only the supplement (the catch-up is earlier-year only).
    - initial payment <- first-installment duplicate refund: only that refund (the general refund refuses a current-year first installment).
    - initial payment <- credit: only the credit policy writes credits.
  - Each exclusion is a scope sentence and a 0/1 binding checked in result; checked by evaluating all eight policies on both worlds' holdings (task 0's account: task 1's three policies figure 0; task 1's new enrollment: the catch-up is out of scope, and the draft, one-time payment and duplicate refund figure 0).
- Robustness: dr_late_amt / rf_late_amt default to 0 where an installment carries no payment.
- A first attempt put a reinstatement exclusion on the initial payment (appeal read); check_compute rejected it because task 1's world seeds no appeal holding, so the exclusion moved to the catch-up's plan-year scope instead.
- Scored values, factor sensitivities and load-bearing figures unchanged; six orders per task give one hash. Prerequisite sentences unchanged this round. Rationale scope cards in both tasks state the plan-year split. task_tools.py unchanged. Full gate block green including check_traceability (22/0 and 21/0).
